title: Perf run 20261022-0341
heading: The side choice's scene on a phone 18% sooner, and the reopened computer game's board 8% sooner
meta: This speed run kept two changes. The build now asks V8 to compile the 3D scene's code as it downloads, off the main thread (CH1). The side choice now prepares its shaders before its first frame, with the page free meanwhile (SL1). On the final code (17f97eb), measured against the base a2bac8d over 10 pairs, two primary rows are called better and none worse: the side choice's scene on a phone went from 2.30 s to 1.88 s (×0.817), and the reopened computer game's board on a phone from 2.45 s to 2.24 s (×0.923). The cost is memory: the JS heap after reopening a 2,000-ply game is 3.7% larger, and that row leans 5% slower, though not called. Both are under “Needs from me”. The branch is improve/20261022-0341. Main did not move during the run. Every figure comes from software rendering (SwiftShader) on a 4-vCPU VM, and each one names the commits it compares.

needs.intro: No call of taste this run. The two items are information that the speed rule and the memory flag ask for.

items.title: The compile hint costs 3.7% heap, and reopening a long game leans 5% slower
items.body:
Information, not a question. In the final A/B (ab-20261022-0341-final.md), "Reopening a long game (2,000 plies)" is 116 → 119 ms, ×1.054 at the median pair, with 8 of 10 pairs worse (pairs 0.86–1.21). It is not called. The JS heap after that reopen went from 14,637 to 15,186 KiB (+3.7%), with every pair between 1.03 and 1.05. That is below the 5% memory flag.

An A/A of the base against itself on the same section, 12 pairs (ab-20261022-0341-aa-reopen.md), reads the long reopen ×0.954 and the heap +0.1%. So the heap rise comes from the change: code that V8 compiles up front stays on the heap. The long reopen leaned ×1.04–1.07 in all four A/Bs that included the hint, and not in the A/A. So the lean is likely the change too, about 3–6 ms on a 116 ms moment. In return, the side choice on a phone saves 420 ms and the reopened computer game's board on a phone saves 210 ms.

items.title: Two more primary rows are over 3% worse at the median; neither is called
items.body:
Information, not a question. In the final A/B:

  • A picked-up piece appears: 75.0 → 78.8 ms, ×1.091, 6 of 10 pairs worse (pairs 0.83–1.40). Run 2131's A/A of identical code read this row ×1.048 with 8 of 12 pairs worse. Neither change runs on a pick: the code is compiled by then, and no program links (0 on both sides).
  • First board picture, playing the computer: 922 → 933 ms, ×1.033, 6 of 10 pairs worse (pairs 0.92–1.24). Its section's other rows did not move.
items.recommend: Merge. Ledger item 2131:NF1, a verdict that judges each row against its own A/A spread, would settle such leans.

scoreboard.intro: The primary rows are the moments a player waits for, listed in bench/primary.mjs. Each bar is a row's change, head divided by base, and each dot is one pair. Left of 1× is faster. The dashed line is the target, 1.2× faster than the base.

items.title: The final code against the base: all 20 primary rows
items.body:
17f97eb against a2bac8d, 10 pairs, 79 minutes (ab-20261022-0341-final.md). The later commits change only the loop's records. Overall the head is ×1.009 as fast as the base, against ×1.004 for identical code. Called better: the side choice's scene on a phone, 2.30 → 1.88 s (×0.817, pairs 0.80–0.86), and the computer's game reopened on a phone, its board, 2.45 → 2.24 s (×0.923, pairs 0.89–0.98). Nothing is called worse. Every load downloads the same bytes as on the base (+0.2 KiB, the hint's comment). Live geometries and textures did not change.

Five diagnostics are called better, none worse. The start page's first click now draws the lobby's scene in about half the time on a desktop (523 → 263 ms) and 24% sooner on a phone (1.43 → 1.08 s). The desktop start page spends 40 ms running script until it is ready, down from 94 ms. The side choice's words still come in with its scene, and the lobby never fell back to its 1.5 s timer.

The 1.2× target is met by one row only: the side choice on a phone (×0.817). The other rows wait mostly on the GPU or the network, which these changes don't touch.

changed.intro: Each change is its own commit, measured by an interleaved A/B. The final A/B above measures both together on every primary row.

items.title: V8 compiles the scene's code as it downloads (CH1, a2ecc5a)
items.body:
V8 normally compiles a function on the main thread the first time it runs. A comment, //# allFunctionsCalledOnLoad, as a script's first line asks it to compile the whole file while it streams in, on a background thread. The build now puts that line on every chunk that no first screen loads statically: three.js, the canvases, the scene's parts, the piece data and the search's main-thread fallback. That is 11 chunks. The entry and the pages' own chunks don't get it, because on a fast network compiling them up front is what the first screen waits on (the rejected form below). A phone trace of /new shows the main thread's compiling falling from 260–280 ms to about 100 ms.

Against a2bac8d, setup, computer and reopen, 12 pairs (ab-20261022-0341-ch1.md): the reopened computer game's board on a phone, 2.41 → 2.23 s (×0.929), called better. That A/B measured 8 of the 20 primary rows. The final A/B measures all 20 with both changes. vite.config.test.ts checks the hint is line 1, after Vite's own first line, that no first screen's chunk gets it, and that the build fails if three.js lands in a first screen's chunk.

items.title: The side choice prepares its shaders before its first frame (SL1, a5341e3)
items.body:
The lobby's canvas on the side choice (/new, /computer) now hands its shaders to the GPU before its first frame and waits for them with the page free, as the game's board and the start page's preview already do (linkBeforeFirstFrame). Before, the first frame linked them itself and held the page. A shared game's invitation keeps the old path, because its Join click would find the GPU still busy (run 0411's J1). The words still come in with the scene's first frame.

Against a2ecc5a, setup and computer, 8 pairs (ab-20261022-0341-sl1.md): the side choice's scene on a phone, 2.15 → 1.86 s (×0.864), called better. That A/B measured 7 of the 20 primary rows. The final A/B measures all 20. showcase.mjs --lobby on 17f97eb shows the entrance as before: black at 0 s, then the words, platform and kings fading up together.

items.body: One sentence names the side choice among the canvases that link ahead, and one paragraph says which chunks carry the compile hint and why the first screens' chunks don't. The plugin's comment now says the same.

rejected.intro: Each rejected form is in the ledger with its report or patch.

items.title: The compile hint on every chunk, the entry and the worker included
items.body: Against a2bac8d, all primary rows, 8 pairs (ab-20261022-0341-ch1-all.md, patch patches/0341-CH1-every-chunk.patch). Two phone rows were called better: the side choice ×0.945 and the reopened computer game's turn ×0.940. But the desktop shared game's first screen read ×1.182 (7 of 8 pairs worse), and desktop DOMContentLoaded (+18%) and the JS heap (+5.7%) were called worse. On a fast network, compiling a first screen's chunk up front is what the page waits on. The kept form leaves those chunks out.

items.title: The compile hint on the three.js chunk alone
items.body: Two exploratory A/Bs, not committed (8 and 12 pairs). The side choice on a phone read ×0.929 and ×0.949, and the reopened computer game's board ×0.952 and ×0.960, better in nearly every pair but never called. Widening the hint to every scene chunk made the board's row called (the kept form).

choices.intro: Decisions made without you, to overrule if you disagree.

items.title: The compile hint stays off the first screens' chunks
items.body: The every-chunk form helped two phone rows and hurt the desktop first screens. Trading a desktop first screen for a phone's is your kind of call, so it is parked as a patch, not proposed.

items.title: SL1 follows the lobby's beat, not the route
items.body: The canvas links ahead when it is created on the side choice's beat (choose), which covers /new and /computer. A shared game's invitation keeps today's path.

items.title: Commit messages left as written
items.body: Both perf commits say "no primary row called worse" from A/Bs that measured 8 and 7 of the 20 rows. Rewording them would mean rewriting pushed history. The final A/B measures all 20 rows and calls none worse, and the PR says which rows each A/B measured.

items.title: Review items logged, not fixed
items.body: This is a speed run, so the review's checks and cleanups went to the ledger: a test pinning SL1's beat split (0341:LT1), a check of the hint in the real build (HB1), the lobby's 1.5 s fallback on slow phones (LL1), the entrance's first step (FE1), the hint outside the chunk's hash (HC1) and one first-screen walk for two plugins (FW1).

items.title: Returning visitors and the compile hint
items.body: The hint is added after the build names each chunk by its content's hash, so it does not change the name. A returning browser that already holds an unchanged chunk keeps its cached copy without the hint until that chunk next changes. The bench builds a fresh cache on each side, so it cannot see this (ledger 0341:HC1).

items.title: Real phones and other browsers
items.body: The hint is a V8 feature: Firefox and Safari ignore the comment. Every figure is from Chromium's headless shell with software rendering and a throttled CPU, not a real phone's GPU.
